textbookText: Stimulus or cause of migration i. Though exact cause of bird migration is unknown, some factor which stimulate bird migration are listed in points below: ii. Intensity of light stimulates the gonad affecting nervous system bringing migration. iii. Scarcity of food, shortening day length, increase in coldness or hotness etc. in certain area causes migration. iv. Many birds show restlessness after the deposition of fat in their body followed by migration.

Types of migration in birds 1. Latitudinal: It is the type of migration of bird which occurs from northern hemisphere to southern hemisphere and vice versa. Golden plover of USA migrate to south i.e. Argentina; Siberian birds migrate to plains of Himalayas in India and Nepal. 2. Longitudinal: Migration of birds from east to west and vice versa is called longitudinal migration. E.g. Starling bird move from East Europe or Asia to the Atlantic coast. 3. Altitudinal migration: Migration of birds which takes place from higher altitude to lower altitude and vice versa. Example: wood cock, bush chat, Violet green swallows of U.K, Lophophorus in Nepal. 4. Vagrant migration: Some birds from their home migrate in all direction to a long distance for food and protection from enemies called vagrant or irregular migration. Herons after breeding migrate in this way.

Figure: 9.2.11 some migratory birds 5. Seasonal migration: Migration of bird related to seasonal changes. E.g. Nightingales, swifts, cuckoos etc. are summer visitors but snow bunting, and redwings are winter visitors. 6. Daily migration: Daily movement of bird from their nest in response to light, temperature, food. For E.g. sparrow, crow etc.

Mode of flight during migration Birds migrating at night are called nocturnal migrants and those at day time are called diurnal migrants. Common nocturnal migrants are thrushes, night hawk, owl, nightjar etc. and diurnal migrants are crow, swallow, robins, pelican, etc. At the time migration some birds travel in separate companies and some birds in mixed companies. Distance travelled by birds depends on the local climatic condition and species of bird. Himalayan snow partridges descend hardly about one or two mile distance whereas European white stork covers 8000 miles. Smaller bird fly close to earth within about 3000 feet from earth surface and some species of birds even cross Andes and the Himalayas at the altitude of 20000 feet or more. Birds usually travel 5-6 hours a day resting in between for food and water. Migratory birds usually follow definite lines of flight. Nocturnal migrants proceed with general airflow on a broad front. Birds take reference of configuration of land, coastline, course of Great River, intervening mountains chain, position of celestial bodies, constellation during migration.

Advantages i. It helps to protect bird from harsh climatic condition. ii. This phenomenon helps bird to find breeding ground. iii. It prevents overcrowding of birds in the particular area and helps to exploit food and other resources from new or untouched places. iv. It ensures better chance of survival of young ones from predator in the migrated place.

Disadvantages i. At the long journey of migration, some birds may be excessively tired and may fall down on sea, river, forest, rocks and die. ii. There is a high risk of natural enemies during migration. iii. Various natural calamities like heavy rain, snow fall, storms, hurricane etc may be the cause of death for many migratory birds. iv. Several parasitic infections may occur at the time of migration.
